Strait of Hormuz Status: October 15, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  228 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
15 October 2026 .
Brent $ 105.38 -1.12 % · Transits 2 (2026-10-11) · AI-assisted
01 The Guardian reports Iranian attacks have sunk two ships in the Strait of Hormuz as attacks sharpen.

02 Brent stood at $105.38, down 1.12% over 24 hours, as of 00:16 UTC.

03 IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic, and the operational picture darkened further as The Guardian reports that Iranian attacks have sunk two ships in or near the strait, with The New York Times reporting attacks on ships there have escalated sharply. The Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride, already in earlier reporting, is among the vessels involved: MarineLink reports the Maritime and Port Authority of Middle East Eye said it was struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the strait. Separately, Bloomberg reports a cargo ship sank after a strike caused a fire, reported on October 14, and The Guardian and The Washington Post report two ships have now sunk near the strait amid a surge in Iranian attacks. Iran, per Al Jazeera relaying an Iranian claim, vows to fight until the United States accepts its demands. On the tactical picture, The Japan Times reports Iran is shifting tactics to step up attacks on shipping. On the US military side, gCaptain and the Jerusalem Post report US forces destroyed an Iranian-affiliated dhow in the Gulf of Oman on October 6 after determining it was conducting surveillance and helping target American warships. IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day; 111 headlines have been indexed in the last 24 hours. Brent was at $105.38, down 1.12% over 24 hours, as of 00:16 UTC. As of 00:22 UTC, 151 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
